message.content: Harbor has to open with no network. Where should everything a person has seen be kept?

content.text: Two shapes are worth weighing: an embedded file, or a bundled server such as Postgres. Which way do you lean?

message.content: Try bundling Postgres and see how it starts.

content.text: The bundled Postgres cluster takes four seconds to initialize on first launch and needs a free port, and the sandbox refuses its shared memory segment.

message.content: Forget that. A server process on a laptop is one more thing to fail at launch. Go with SQLite.

content.text: Then it is **one SQLite file per account** in write-ahead-log mode, with a single writer task, so readers never block the interface. Remote storage is out too, because it is exactly what is missing when the store is needed.

Gate the schema on `PRAGMA user_version` with a list of numbered migrations. A migration that fails leaves the old file in place and starts the app **read-only**, so nothing a person has is lost and they can still look at it.

content.content:
pub const SCHEMA_VERSION: i64 = 3;
pub const MIGRATIONS: &[(i64, &str)] = &[(1, ADD_NOTES), (2, ADD_REVISIONS), (3, ADD_ACCOUNTS)];

content.text: The list is already in that shape at version 3, so only the failure path is new.
